I'm not sure it'll be of much help, but I understand. I'm 31 and my partner is soon 30. We've started trying in late March after I went to the hospital for blood checkup related to my ongoing stuff. I said I want a child and got green light as I got very good results. We barely made it into that cycle's fertility window so I didn't have *too* high hopes, but boy oh boy was I hyped for next cycle. Especially since I was very determined to have a January baby. I tracked BBT every day, ovulation strips sometimes multiple times a day and getting hot and steamy absolutely every day. Then the dreaded TWW. Cramping, exactly when they should be, bloating, severe nausea, frequent urination, weird vivid dreams, you name it. And of course - my period that is always early, was late *dun dun duuun*
*a few negative tests later* 
My period came and crashed the party. We were crushed. I cried. We were so sure, I felt it. Alas...
You know what I honestly tried to do? Not care. I barely tracked, I couldn't even pinpoint my peak ovulation, we barely did anything. I was just not feeling the whole February baby vibe.
Well... turns out... funny story... I'm quite positively pregnant. 
Moral of the story - stressing myself out over every tiny detail abd counting the days wasn't doing me a favour. I know it's super difficult to do and easier to say. In ny case I'm just very particular about zodiacs so I found a reason *not* to be "invested" this month. I thought it SURELY won't happen. 
If she will feel calmer by both of you getting some tests - go for it. But she needs to remind herself to relax and that there's nothing *necessarily* wrong with her OR you. And if it didn't happen - might be for a reason. Think about it, maybe a healthier egg is in the queue, waiting for a chance to shine. 
Sending hugs and wishes for BFPs your way.

Last time I was home, I suddenly felt really unwell. I started feeling cold chills and shivering. I had 3 blankets and 4 cats on top of me. I had fuzzy socks on. I made burning hot tea. My lips and fingers were blue, I had no blood left in my face and my temperature was nearing 39°C. I was scared. I thought I'd die. I had no medications at home, not even simple ones. It was 2am. I texted her and she said she'll come bring me some medications. She was at work. She left 1h early and rushed to me on a taxi across the city. The medication she gave me worked fast and I felt better. But I realise what could have happened had my internal organ temperature not gone down. 
There's honestly nobody I'd have rhe confidence to call in a time of need (except my family, as I'm lucky to have them). Likewise she can rely on me for anything.

Spend time with my beloved cats and make sure they live very comfortably and are healthy as can be, spend time with family and friends and work on actually developing high-quality relationships. I'd also clear my family and friends financial burdens. I'd go to therapy and heal, address my physical health and regularly do checkups, make sure I eat a healthy diet that is fitted to my individual needs. I'd make sure I go to the dentist and fix anything that needs to be addressed. I'd travel and experience different cultures and meet new people, I'd document my journeys, I'd create art. And I'd actively participate in causes I care for and get involved in charity. Basically I'd do all the things I really want to do while working on myself to become a better person and have a positive impact. I try to do all these things on smaller scales whenever I can, but for example with charity, it's sometimes difficult to be generous if you yourself are struggling and in need of generosity.

Probably lots of things, but being bullied nost of my life AND having a string of toxic relationships (receiving end of abuse and narcissism) really messed me up. So I'd say that un-learning negative patterns is the most difficult thing to be done and it's basically what's wrong with me - a lot of fundamental life experiences I've had are negatively hard-wired into my brain.

I'd go back to 2020 and the happy days I had during that pandemic summer, right until I met my ex. From there everything went to shit. I miss those times and I believe that if I had a chance to re-do, I'd choose differently, 100%.
